q: What did Monconys see at Kuffler's house in London in 1663?
label: after
final:
Balthasar de Monconys visited the Kuffler family—the heirs to Cornelis Drebbel’s secrets—to witness the remnants of Drebbel's extraordinary mechanical and alchemical inventions, including his "perpetual motion" machine and his famous self-regulating oven.

In June 1663, the French traveler Balthasar de Monconys visited the London home of **Johannes Siberius Kuffler**, the son-in-law of the famous Dutch inventor **Cornelis Drebbel**. Monconys was a keen observer of the "new science" and went specifically to see the remnants of Drebbel’s legendary inventions, which the Kuffler family guarded as trade secrets.

According to his *Journal des Voyages*, Monconys saw several remarkable devices:

### The Self-Regulating Oven (Athanor)
Monconys provided a detailed description and a diagram of Drebbel's famous "secret" furnace. This was an early thermostat-controlled oven designed for alchemical or chemical work. It used a **mercury register** to maintain a constant temperature:
> *A quotation stood here that I could not find on any page I read, so I removed it.*

### The Naval "Engine" (Explosive Mine)
Kuffler showed Monconys a device intended for naval warfare—essentially a primitive torpedo or mine. It consisted of a box about 9 inches square filled with a "powder" (likely including fulminating gold) attached to a 20-foot pole. Kuffler claimed it could blow up a ship on contact without harming the person deploying it. This "engine" had been demonstrated to Oliver Cromwell, but negotiations with the Crown had stalled after his death. — *[Oud Holland, jaargang 22 (1904)](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/oud-holland-jaargang-22-1904-various)* by Various, [Page 304](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/oud-holland-jaargang-22-1904-various/page-number/304).

### The Perpetual Motion Machine
Monconys also sought to see Drebbel's most famous invention: a "perpetual motion" clock or globus. This device was said to be driven by changes in atmospheric pressure and temperature (acting on a liquid in a tube), which Drebbel claimed mirrored the "macrocosm" in a "microcosm." While the original grand version given to King James I had been damaged or lost, the Kufflers still held the principles and smaller models of the device.

### Bread and "Drebbel's Scarlet"
The Kufflers were also known for their commercial application of Drebbel’s chemical discoveries. They operated a successful dye-works using "Drebbel’s Scarlet" (a brilliant red dye made using tin and cochineal) and even a specialized bakery using Drebbel's regulated ovens. Monconys noted the family's earnestness in trying to sell these "engines" to various European powers, including Christiaan Huygens and the French court. — *[Complete Works, Volume 4: Correspondence 1662-1663](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/oeuvres-completes-tome-4-correspondance-1662-1663-huygens)* by [Christiaan Huygens](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/christiaan-huygens), [Page 411](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/oeuvres-completes-tome-4-correspondance-1662-1663-huygens/page-number/411).

You might explore the technical diagrams of Drebbel's furnace in the *Journal des Voyages*, or read Samuel Pepys's contemporary account of meeting "the German Dr. Kuffler" to discuss his ship-destroying inventions.

q: How did Drebbel's self-regulating oven work, and who described it after his death?
label: after
final:
Cornelis Drebbel’s furnace, often considered the first automated thermostat, used the expansion of air to move a column of mercury, which in turn regulated a damper to maintain a constant temperature for alchemical or incubatory purposes.

Cornelis Drebbel’s self-regulating furnace, often called an "athanor" or "philosophical furnace," functioned as the world's first feedback-controlled thermostat. After his death in 1633, the secret of its construction was maintained by his family, particularly his sons-in-law, the Kuffler brothers, who demonstrated it to the leading scientific minds of the 17th century.

### How the Oven Worked
The mechanism relied on the thermal expansion of air and the weight of mercury. Inside the furnace, a glass tube containing air was connected to a U-shaped vessel filled with mercury. As the furnace heated up, the air in the tube expanded, pushing the mercury. This movement of mercury would either lift or lower a float connected to a rod. This rod, in turn, was linked to a damper (a mechanical valve) that controlled the air supply to the fire. 

When the furnace became too hot, the expanding air pushed the mercury to close the damper, starving the fire of oxygen and cooling the system. Conversely, as it cooled, the air contracted, the mercury receded, and the damper opened to revive the flame. This allowed for a "constant heat" (ignis constans) essential for long-term alchemical digestions or the incubation of eggs.

### Posthumous Descriptions
Following Drebbel's death, several notable figures documented the device:

*   **The Kuffler Family:** Drebbel's sons-in-law, Abraham and Johannes Sibertus Kuffler, continued to use and promote the furnace. Samuel Sorbière, in his 1666 account of his travels to England, mentions seeing a furnace belonging to "Mr. Kuffler, son-in-law of Drebbel," which could "open and close its own dampers according to whether it needs more or less heat" — *[Relation d'un voyage en Angleterre](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/relation-dun-voyage-en-angleterre-ou-sont-touchees-plusieurs-choses-qu)* by [Samuel Sorbière](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/samuel-sorbiere), [Page 68](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/relation-dun-voyage-en-angleterre-ou-sont-touchees-plusieurs-choses-qu?page=68).
*   **Balthasar de Monconys:** The French diplomat and traveler Monconys provided one of the most detailed technical descriptions and drawings of the furnace after visiting the Kufflers in the 1660s. He noted its use for both alchemy and the hatching of chickens.
*   **Robert Boyle and the Royal Society:** The early Royal Society took a keen interest in Drebbel’s "secret." Boyle and others discussed the "Drebbelian" method of temperature control as a precursor to modern experimental chemistry.

![A detailed woodcut of an athanor, a self-feeding furnace used to maintain constant heat.](https://images.sourcelibrary.org/archived/69bd9cb16120d54bd03705ed/262.jpg)
*A 'furnus fixatorius' or athanor from [In hoc vo lumine De alchemia](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/in-hoc-vo-lumine-de-alchemia-continentur-haec-de-ibn-haiyan-2), [Page 262](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/in-hoc-vo-lumine-de-alchemia-continentur-haec-de-ibn-haiyan-2?page=262).*

![An engraving of an athanor topped with a phoenix, symbolizing the constant heat of the Great Work.](https://images.sourcelibrary.org/pages/69a0278d6bc332f148ccf4a4/0352-full.jpg)
*The 'Usus Athanoris' from [The Triple Chemical Torch](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/taeda-trifida-chimica-das-ist-dreyfache-chimische-fackel-dienheim), [Page 352](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/taeda-trifida-chimica-das-ist-dreyfache-chimische-fackel-dienheim?page=352).*

You might explore how Drebbel applied these same pneumatic principles to his famous "perpetual motion" machine, or look into the Kufflers' development of "Drebbel’s Scarlet" dye, which Samuel Sorbière also observed during his travels.

q: What does Drebbel's treatise on the nature of the elements say about heat and cold?
label: after
final:
In his 1604 treatise *Ein kurtzer Tractat von der Natur der Elementen* (A Short Treatise on the Nature of the Elements), Cornelis Drebbel presents heat and cold not merely as temperatures, but as the primary active forces that drive the mechanical motion of the entire cosmos.

### Heat as Expansion and Life
Drebbel defines heat as the principle of **rarefaction** and **expansion**. He argues that heat makes all things "subtle" and "thin," allowing them to rise and move. In his view, fire is the "life" of the elements; without it, the other three elements (air, water, and earth) would remain "dead" and motionless.

> "For just as the fire is the life and lives in the air, so the air also lives in the fire... the fire makes all things subtle."
— *[Ein kurtzer Tractat von der Natur der Elementen](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/ein-kurtzer-tractat-von-der-natur-der-elementen-drebbel)* by [Cornelis Jacobsz Drebbel](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/drebbel-cornelis-jacobsz), [Page 14](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/ein-kurtzer-tractat-von-der-natur-der-elementen-drebbel/page-number/14)

### Cold as Contraction and Fixation
Conversely, Drebbel identifies cold as the principle of **contraction** and **condensation**. Cold is an "effect of the earth" that makes elements "coarse," thick, and hard. It is the force that pulls the elements back into themselves, causing them to shrink and settle.

> "For just as heat makes air and water subtle, thin, and coarse, so cold, as an opposite of heat, makes coarse, shrinks, and presses together."
— *[Ein kurtzer Tractat von der Natur der Elementen](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/ein-kurtzer-tractat-von-der-natur-der-elementen-drebbel)* by [Cornelis Jacobsz Drebbel](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/drebbel-cornelis-jacobsz), [Page 17](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/ein-kurtzer-tractat-von-der-natur-der-elementen-drebbel/page-number/17)

### The Mechanical Proof: The Retort Experiment
Drebbel offers a specific physical experiment to prove this theory, which became the foundation for his famous "perpetual motion" machine and early thermometers. He instructs the reader to take a glass retort, submerge its neck in water, and heat the "belly" of the glass. 

![A woodcut from Drebbel's 1608 treatise illustrating the expansion of air when heated.](https://images.sourcelibrary.org/archived/6a9058b07f6818cc17cd5a93/17.jpg)
*This woodcut from Cornelis Drebbel's 1608 treatise on the elements illustrates a physical experiment designed to demonstrate the properties of air and heat. From [Ein kurtzer Tractat von der Natur der Elementen](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/ein-kurtzer-tractat-von-der-natur-der-elementen-drebbel), [Page 17](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/ein-kurtzer-tractat-von-der-natur-der-elementen-drebbel/page-number/17).*

As the air inside the glass warms, it expands and escapes as bubbles through the water. When the heat is removed, the air goes back into itself (contracts), and the water is sucked up into the retort to fill the space. Drebbel notes that air can be "released and enlarged" by heat many thousands of times its original volume.

### Meteorological and Biological Effects
Drebbel uses this mechanical model to explain all natural phenomena:
*   **Wind:** Caused by the massive expansion of air when warmed by the sun.
*   **Rain:** Caused when warm, expanded air reaches the "thick, dense, and cold air" of the upper atmosphere, where it is "pressed together" and changed back into water.
*   **Growth:** In plants, the warmth of the sun draws the "spirits" of the earth and water upward through the stalks, while cold "congeals" these fluids into solid form.

![A portrait of Cornelis Drebbel, the "Philosopher of Alkmaar."](https://images.sourcelibrary.org/archived/6a9058b07f6818cc17cd5a93/4.jpg)
*Engraving of the Dutch inventor Cornelis Drebbel (1572–1633). From [Ein kurtzer Tractat von der Natur der Elementen](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/ein-kurtzer-tractat-von-der-natur-der-elementen-drebbel), [Page 4](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/ein-kurtzer-tractat-von-der-natur-der-elementen-drebbel/page-number/4).*

q: How does the Poimandres describe the creation of man?
label: after
final:
The *Poimandres* describes the creation of Man (the *Anthropos*) not as a molding of clay, but as the birth of a divine, celestial being who is the very image of the Father and shares in his creative power — *[Corpus Hermeticum with Pneumatica and Ocellus Lucanus](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/corpus-hermeticum-with-pneumatica-and-ocellus-lucanus-alexandria)*, [Page 156](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/corpus-hermeticum-with-pneumatica-and-ocellus-lucanus-alexandria/page-number/156).

In the *Poimandres*—the first tractate of the *Corpus Hermeticum*—the creation of man is a cosmic drama of divine reflection, descent, and the mingling of spirit with matter. Unlike the biblical account of a craftsman shaping clay, the Hermetic "Man" (*Anthropos*) is a celestial being of pure Light and Life who is the equal of his Creator — *[The Hermetic Writings, Volume I: Texts and Translation](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/hermetica-vol-i-texts-and-translation-ed)*, [Page 124](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/hermetica-vol-i-texts-and-translation-ed/page-number/124).

### The Birth of the Divine Man
The narrative begins with the Divine Mind (*Nous*), described as "Life and Light," begetting a Man like unto Himself. This Man was not an earthly creature but a divine archetype — *[The Hermetic Writings, Volume I: Texts and Translation](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/hermetica-vol-i-texts-and-translation-ed)*, [Page 124](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/hermetica-vol-i-texts-and-translation-ed/page-number/124).

> "But Mind the Father of all, he who is Life and Light, gave birth to Man, a Being like to Himself. And He took delight in Man, as being His own offspring; for Man was very goodly to look on, bearing the likeness of his Father. With good reason then did God take delight in Man; for it was God’s own form that God took delight in. And God delivered over to Man all things that had been made."
— *[The Hermetic Writings, Volume I: Texts and Translation](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/hermetica-vol-i-texts-and-translation-ed)* by [Walter Scott (ed.)](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/walter-scott), [Page 125](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/hermetica-vol-i-texts-and-translation-ed?page=125)

The Man, having observed the creation of the "Demiurge" (the second Mind who fashioned the seven planetary spheres), wished to create for himself. His Father granted him permission, and as he passed through the spheres, the seven Governors (the planetary spirits) fell in love with him, each giving him a share of their own nature — *[The Hermetic Writings, Volume I: Texts and Translation](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/hermetica-vol-i-texts-and-translation-ed)*, [Page 124](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/hermetica-vol-i-texts-and-translation-ed/page-number/124).

q: What did Gaspar Ens write about Drebbel's perpetual motion instrument?
label: after
final:
Gaspar Ens, in his 1636 work *Thaumaturgus Mathematicus* (The Mathematical Wonder-worker), was among the first to categorize [Cornelis Drebbel](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/cornelius-drebbel)’s famous "perpetual motion" machine as a scientific instrument for measuring temperature — *[Oud Holland, jaargang 22 (1904)](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/oud-holland-jaargang-22-1904-various)*, [Page 270](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/oud-holland-jaargang-22-1904-various/page-number/270).

### The Drebbelian Instrument
Ens identified the device not as a true mechanical perpetual motion machine, but as an improved "weather glass" or thermometer. He titled his description:

> "De thermometro Sive instrumento Drebiliano quo gradus caloris et frigoris aëre occupante explorantur" 
> (On the thermometer or Drebbelian instrument by which degrees of heat and cold are explored by means of the air occupying it). 
— *[Oud Holland, jaargang 22 (1904)](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/oud-holland-jaargang-22-1904-various)* by [Various](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/unknown), [Page 294](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/oud-holland-jaargang-22-1904-various?page=294)

Ens provided two drawings of this improved weather glass, noting that it functioned by the expansion and contraction of air. While [Drebbel](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/cornelius-drebbel) himself marketed the device to King James I as a "perpetual motion" (*mobilis perpetui*) that could track the heavens and the tides forever, Ens and later scholars like Samuel Reyher noted that this "motion" was actually a natural reaction to atmospheric changes.

### Mechanism and Reception
The instrument consisted of a glass globe or tube containing "deep red water" and air. As the ambient temperature changed, the air inside would expand or contract, moving the liquid and thereby driving the clockwork or display.

![engraving of Drebbel's Perpetuum Mobile](https://images.sourcelibrary.org/archived/6ac2799102c7f994f8506bef/268.jpg)
*The 'Perpetuum Mobile' presented by Drebbel to King James I, from [Oud Holland, jaargang 22 (1904)](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/oud-holland-jaargang-22-1904-various), [Page 268](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/oud-holland-jaargang-22-1904-various?page=268).*

Ens's inclusion of the device in his *[The Mathematical Thaumaturge](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/thaumaturgus-mathematicus-id-est-admirabilium-effectorum-e-ens)* positioned it alongside other "mathematical recreations" and wonders of the age. His account helped bridge the gap between the occult "perpetual motion" of the Renaissance and the empirical "thermometer" of the Scientific Revolution. Other contemporary authors, such as [Gaspar Schott](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/gaspar-schott), drew upon Ens's work to discuss the distinction between "artificial" perpetual motion (which many deemed impossible) and "natural" motion driven by the elements.

You might explore [Drebbel's own letter to King James I](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/drebbel-tractatus-duo-1628-latin-laurembergius?page=62) for his original claims, or examine [Athanasius Kircher's critiques](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/magnes-sive-de-arte-magnetica-kircher?page=407) of such "natural" perpetual motion devices.

q: What does the Emerald Tablet say, and which editions of it do you have?
label: after
final:
The Emerald Tablet, or *Tabula Smaragdina*, is the foundational text of Western alchemy, traditionally attributed to the legendary sage Hermes Trismegistus. It famously articulates the principle of correspondence—"as above, so below"—establishing the link between the macrocosm and the microcosm — *[Amphitheatre of Eternal Wisdom (1609)](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/amphitheatre-of-eternal-wisdom-1609-khunrath)*, [Page 267](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/amphitheatre-of-eternal-wisdom-1609-khunrath/page-number/267).

### The Text of the Emerald Tablet
The tablet consists of thirteen or fourteen succinct, enigmatic precepts. In [Heinrich Khunrath](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/heinrich-khunrath)’s 1609 *[Amphitheatre of Eternal Wisdom](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/amphitheatre-of-eternal-wisdom-1609-khunrath)*, the Latin text is rendered as follows:

> 1. True without lie, most certain, and highest truth:
> 2. That which is below is as that which is above, and that which is above, is as that which is below, to perpetuate the miracles of the one thing.
> 3. And just as all things were produced from one, by the meditation of the one: so all things were born from this one thing by adaptation.
> 4. Its father is the Sun, its mother the Moon; the wind carried it in its belly; its nurse is the earth.
> 5. The father of every completion (*telesmi*) of the whole world is here; its power is complete if it be turned into earth.
> 6. You shall separate the earth from the fire, the subtle from the dense, gently, with great skill and wisdom.
> 7. It ascends from the earth to the heaven, and again it descends to the earth and receives the power of the higher and the lower things.
> 8. Thus you shall have the glory of the whole world. Therefore all obscurity will flee from you.
> 9. This is the strength of all strength, because it will conquer every subtle thing, and will penetrate every solid thing.
> 10. Thus the world was created.
> 11. Hence there will be marvelous adaptations, the manner of which is here.
> 12. Therefore I have been called Hermes Trismegistus, having three parts of the philosophy of the whole world.
> 13. What I have said concerning the operation of the Sun is finished.
> — *[Amphitheatre of Eternal Wisdom](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/amphitheatre-of-eternal-wisdom-1609-khunrath)*, [Page 267](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/amphitheatre-of-eternal-wisdom-1609-khunrath?page=267)

### Notable Editions in the Collection
Our library holds **34 books** explicitly authored by or attributed to [Hermes Trismegistus](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/hermes-trismegistus), and the Emerald Tablet appears in numerous alchemical compendiums across the centuries:

*   **Early Printed Editions**: One of the earliest appearances in our catalog is in a 1541 edition of the *[Tabula Smaragdina](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/tabula-smaragdina-trismegistus)*.
*   **Alchemical Compendiums**: The text is a cornerstone of major works like [Salomon Trismosin](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/salomon-trismosin)’s *[Aureum Vellus](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/aureum-vellus-splendor-solis-golden-fleece-trismosin)* (1598), where it is described as being found by Hermes in a cave in the Valley of Hebron, carved on marble pillars [Page 471](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/aureum-vellus-splendor-solis-golden-fleece-trismosin?page=471).
*   **Philosophical Commentaries**: It appears with extensive commentary in [Friedrich Roth-Scholtz](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/friedrich-roth-scholtz)’s *[Deutsches theatrum chemicum](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/deutsches-theatrum-chemicum-auf-welchem-der-beruhmtesten-s-n)* (1728) [Page 193](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/deutsches-theatrum-chemicum-auf-welchem-der-beruhmtesten-s-n?page=193) and James Astell's *[Das Fundament der Lehre vom Stein der Weisen](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/das-fundament-der-lehre-vom-stein-der-weisen-oder-des-astell)* (1736) [Page 33](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/das-fundament-der-lehre-vom-stein-der-weisen-oder-des-astell?page=33).
*   **Visual Representations**: The collection includes the famous "Vestigium Veritatis" engraving from [Heinrich Khunrath](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/heinrich-khunrath), which depicts the text inscribed on a massive rock face — *[Amphitheatre of Eternal Wisdom (1609)](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/amphitheatre-of-eternal-wisdom-1609-khunrath)*, [Page 267](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/amphitheatre-of-eternal-wisdom-1609-khunrath/page-number/267).

q: How does Agrippa describe the seal and magic square of Saturn?
label: after
final:
Agrippa describes the **Table of Saturn** (or magic square) as the first of the planetary tables, based on the ternary number three. It consists of a 3x3 grid containing nine particular numbers, arranged so that every row, column, and diagonal sums to **15**, with a total sum of **45** — *[Occult Philosophy](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/de-occulta-philosophia-agrippa-von)*, [Page 185](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/de-occulta-philosophia-agrippa-von/page-number/185).

### The Magic Square (Kamea)
In *De Occulta Philosophia*, Agrippa explains that this square is assigned to Saturn because it is the "highest" and most remote planet, corresponding to the first odd square (3x3). The arrangement of numbers is typically:

| 4 | 9 | 2 |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | 5 | 7 |
| 8 | 1 | 6 |

> "The first of these, assigned to Saturn, consists of a square of three, containing nine particular numbers, and in each line three, and through both diameters constituting fifteen; however, the total sum of the numbers is forty-five."
— *[Occult Philosophy](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/de-occulta-philosophia-agrippa-von)* by [Heinrich Cornelius Agrippa](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/heinrich-cornelius-agrippa), [Page 185](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/de-occulta-philosophia-agrippa-von?page=185).

### The Seal and Sigils
Agriagement separates the planetary symbols into three distinct types, all "elicited" from the numbers of the square:
1.  **The Seal of Saturn:** A geometric pattern formed by connecting the intersections or centers of the square's cells, representing the planet's overall influence — *[La philosophie occulte (De occulta philosophia) Tome 1](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/la-philosophie-occulte-de-occulta-philosophia-tome-1-agrippa)*, [Page 327](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/la-philosophie-occulte-de-occulta-philosophia-tome-1-agrippa/page-number/327).
2.  **The Intelligence of Saturn (Agiel):** A spirit of "good" whose name's Hebrew letters sum to 45 (the total sum of the square). Its sigil is drawn by tracing the path of these numbers on the grid — *[La philosophie occulte (De occulta philosophia) Tome 1](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/la-philosophie-occulte-de-occulta-philosophia-tome-1-agrippa)*, [Page 327](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/la-philosophie-occulte-de-occulta-philosophia-tome-1-agrippa/page-number/327).
3.  **The Spirit of Saturn (Zazel):** A "demon" or spirit of "evil" whose name also sums to 45 — *[La philosophie occulte (De occulta philosophia) Tome 1](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/la-philosophie-occulte-de-occulta-philosophia-tome-1-agrippa)*, [Page 327](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/la-philosophie-occulte-de-occulta-philosophia-tome-1-agrippa/page-number/327). 

![The magic square and planetary seal of Saturn](https://images.sourcelibrary.org/cropped/69c83fc16c6f3cc53c85053b/69f50504f3941bf5188807f2.jpg)
*The magic square and planetary seal of Saturn from Israel Hiebner’s Mysterium sigillorum (1735), [Page 148](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/mysterium-sigillorum-herbarum-lapidum-oder-vollkommene-cur-hiebner-von?page=148).*

![Table of Saturn and its characters](https://images.sourcelibrary.org/archived/69593225b91a6184ea943475/172.jpg)
*Plate from Francis Barrett's The Magus (1801) showing the Kamea of Saturn and the sigils for Agiel and Zazel, [Page 172](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/the-magus-or-celestial-intelligencer-barrett?page=172).*

### Magical Use
According to Agrippa, these characters are engraved on lead (the metal of Saturn) to create talismans. When Saturn is "fortunate" (well-aspected in the sky), the seal is used to help with childbirth, to make a man powerful, or to secure success in petitions. Conversely, if made when Saturn is "unfortunate," it is used to hinder buildings, plantings, or to cause discord and sadness — *[La philosophie occulte Tome 1](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/la-philosophie-occulte-de-occulta-philosophia-tome-1-agrippa)* by [Heinrich Cornelius Agrippa](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/heinrich-cornelius-agrippa), [Page 327](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/la-philosophie-occulte-de-occulta-philosophia-tome-1-agrippa?page=327).

Saved to your research notebook — the *Research notebook* button under the message box on this page opens it.

You might explore how these squares were later analyzed mathematically by **Athanasius Kircher** in his *Arithmologia*, or look into the specific **suffumigations and rituals** Agrippa prescribes to accompany the use of these seals.

1.  **The Seal of Saturn:** A geometric pattern formed by connecting the intersections or centers of the square's cells, representing the planet's overall influence.
2.  **The Intelligence of Saturn (Agiel):** A spirit of "good" whose name's Hebrew letters sum to 45 (the total sum of the square). Its sigil is drawn by tracing the path of these numbers on the grid.
3.  **The Spirit of Saturn (Zazel):** A "demon" or spirit of "evil" whose name also sums to 45. 

![The magic square and planetary seal of Saturn](https://images.sourcelibrary.org/cropped/69c83fc16c6f3cc53c85053b/69f50504f3941bf5188807f2.jpg)
*The magic square and planetary seal of Saturn from Israel Hiebner’s Mysterium sigillorum (1735), [Page 148](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/mysterium-sigillorum-herbarum-lapidum-oder-vollkommene-cur-hiebner-von?page=148).*

![Table of Saturn and its characters](https://images.sourcelibrary.org/archived/69593225b91a6184ea943475/172.jpg)
*Plate from Francis Barrett's The Magus (1801) showing the Kamea of Saturn and the sigils for Agiel and Zazel, [Page 172](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/the-magus-or-celestial-intelligencer-barrett?page=172).*

### Magical Use
According to Agrippa, these characters are engraved on lead (the metal of Saturn) to create talismans. When Saturn is "fortunate" (well-aspected in the sky), the seal is used to help with childbirth, to make a man powerful, or to secure success in petitions. Conversely, if made when Saturn is "unfortunate," it is used to hinder buildings, plantings, or to cause discord and sadness — *[La philosophie occulte Tome 1](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/la-philosophie-occulte-de-occulta-philosophia-tome-1-agrippa)* by [Heinrich Cornelius Agrippa](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/heinrich-cornelius-agrippa), [Page 327](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/la-philosophie-occulte-de-occulta-philosophia-tome-1-agrippa?page=327).

q: What does the Fama Fraternitatis say was found in Christian Rosenkreutz's tomb?
label: after
final:
According to the *Fama Fraternitatis* (1614), the tomb of Father Christian Rosenkreutz was a hidden, seven-sided vault (*heptagon*) discovered by the Brethren 120 years after his death. It was designed as a "compendium of the universe," intended to preserve the Order's entire knowledge even if the brotherhood itself were to perish — *[The Real History of the Rosicrucians](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/the-real-history-of-the-rosicrucians-waite)*, [Page 89](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/the-real-history-of-the-rosicrucians-waite/page-number/89).

### The Vault and the Artificial Sun
The vault was seven-sided, with each side measuring five feet in width and eight feet in height. Although it was deep underground, it was brilliantly illuminated by an artificial "internal sun" located in the center of the ceiling.

> "Although the sun never shone in this vault, it was nonetheless illuminated by another 'sun,' which had learned this light from the actual sun and was situated in the center of the upper part of the ceiling."
— *[The Real History of the Rosicrucians](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/the-real-history-of-the-rosicrucians-waite)* by [Arthur Edward Waite](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/arthur-edward-waite), [Page 89](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/the-real-history-of-the-rosicrucians-waite?page=89)

### The Altar and Inscriptions
In the center of the room stood a circular altar covered with a brass plate. It bore the inscription: *A.C.R.C. Hoc universi compendium unius mihi sepulchrum feci* ("I have made this compendium of the universe my sole tomb"). Around the rim was written *Jesus mihi omnia* ("Jesus is everything to me") — *[The Real History of the Rosicrucians](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/the-real-history-of-the-rosicrucians-waite)*, [Page 89](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/the-real-history-of-the-rosicrucians-waite/page-number/89).

The altar also featured four symbolic figures in circles with the following inscriptions:
1. **Nequaquam Vacuum** (Nowhere a vacuum)
2. **Legis Jugum** (The yoke of the law)
3. **Libertas Evangelii** (The liberty of the Gospel)
4. **Dei gloria intacta** (The glory of God is untouched)

![This illustration depicts the legendary opening of the tomb of…](https://images.sourcelibrary.org/archived/6a35340fc8ce407afbe0518c/5.jpg)
*This illustration depicts the legendary opening of the tomb of Christian Rosenkreuz, the mythical founder of the Rosicrucian Order — [The All-Seeing Eye, Vol. 3 No. 16](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/the-all-seeing-eye-vol-3-no-16-hall), [Page 5](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/the-all-seeing-eye-vol-3-no-16-hall/page-number/5)*

### The Body of C.R.C. and the Book "T."
Upon moving the altar and lifting a heavy brass plate, the Brethren found the body of Christian Rosenkreutz. Despite being buried for over a century, his body was "intact and without any decay." In his hand, he held a small parchment book written in gold, referred to as the **Book T.** (often interpreted as *Testamentum*), which the text describes as the Order's "greatest treasure next to the Bible." — *[Fama Fraternitatis and Confessio Fraternitatis](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/fama-fraternitatis-und-confessio-fraternitatis-rosicrucian)*, [Page 30](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/fama-fraternitatis-und-confessio-fraternitatis-rosicrucian/page-number/30).

> "There, a heavy brass plate could be lifted, and a beautiful and glorious body was found, intact and without any decay... In his hand, he held a little book written on parchment with gold, called T."
— *[Fama Fraternitatis and Confessio Fraternitatis](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/fama-fraternitatis-und-confessio-fraternitatis-rosicrucian)* by [Anonymous (Rosicrucian)](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/anonymous-rosicrucian), [Page 30](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/fama-fraternitatis-und-confessio-fraternitatis-rosicrucian?page=30)

### The Secret Cabinets
The walls of the vault contained secret cabinets filled with objects necessary for the restoration of the Order, including:
*   **Books:** Copies of all the fraternity's secret texts and the *Vocabulario* of Paracelsus — *[The Real History of the Rosicrucians](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/the-real-history-of-the-rosicrucians-waite)*, [Page 90](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/the-real-history-of-the-rosicrucians-waite/page-number/90).
*   **Personal Records:** C.R.C.'s travel diary (*Itinerarium*) and his biography (*Vitam*).
*   **Scientific Instruments:** Mirrors of "various virtues," bells, and burning lamps — *[The Real History of the Rosicrucians](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/the-real-history-of-the-rosicrucians-waite)*, [Page 90](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/the-real-history-of-the-rosicrucians-waite/page-number/90).
*   **Artistic Works:** "Wondrously artificial songs" (*künstliche Gesänge*).

![A group of men in medieval robes kneel in reverence around a circular…](https://images.sourcelibrary.org/cropped/69c874af6c6f3cc53c857cd4/69f6a19d2d87bc4548d51b6f.jpg)
*A group of men in medieval robes kneel in reverence around a circular brass altar inside a stone vault — [An encyclopedic outline of masonic, hermetic, cabbalistic and…](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/an-encyclopedic-outline-of-masonic-hermetic-cabbalistic-and-hall), [Page 219](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/an-encyclopedic-outline-of-masonic-hermetic-cabbalistic-and-hall/page-number/219)*

q: How does Paracelsus describe the tria prima of salt, sulphur and mercury?
label: after

Paracelsus redefined alchemy by introducing the **tria prima**—Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury—as the fundamental principles of all material substance. This triad moved beyond the classical four elements to explain the composition of bodies through their chemical and spiritual properties — *[Philosophy Reformed: Four Profound Tractates](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/philosophy-reformed-four-profound-tractates-paracelsus)*, [Page 81](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/philosophy-reformed-four-profound-tractates-paracelsus/page-number/81).

Paracelsus established the **tria prima**—Mercury, Sulfur, and Salt—as the three "hypostatical" principles that constitute all material things. He argued that while the four classical elements (Earth, Air, Fire, Water) are the "mothers" of things, the tria prima are the actual substances that give bodies their specific qualities and internal "anatomy." — *[Philosophical Works Vol. 3](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/philosophical-works-vol-3-boyle)*, [Page 449](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/philosophical-works-vol-3-boyle/page-number/449).

### The Three Principles and Their Qualities
In the Paracelsian system, these three substances represent the spiritual, soulful, and physical dimensions of matter. A clear breakdown of their properties is provided in Jan Amos Comenius's *Naturall Philosophie Reformed by Divine Light*:

*   **Mercury (Spirit):** Represents fluidity, "coition" (joining together), and rawness. It is incombustible; when exposed to fire, it escapes as vapor.
*   **Sulfur (Soul):** Represents "oiliness," softness, and adhesiveness. It is the principle of inflammability and growth.
*   **Salt (Body):** Represents solidity, hardness, and consistency. It is the principle of "incorruptibility" and fixity; it remains after the other two have been driven off by fire.

> "Principle Qualities Resulting Property:
> **Mercury (☿)** fluidity, coition, rawness. incombustibility.
> **Sulphur** gives unto things softness, adhesiveness, fatness. and from thence inflammability.
> **Salt** consistency, hardness, brittleness. incorruptibility."
> — *[Naturall Philosophie Reformed by Divine Light (1651)](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/naturall-philosophie-reformed-by-divine-light-1651-comenius)* by [Jan Amos Comenius](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/jan-amos-comenius), [Page 103](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/naturall-philosophie-reformed-by-divine-light-1651-comenius?page=103)

### The Analogy of Burning Wood
Paracelsus famously illustrated this doctrine using the example of burning wood. When wood is placed in a fire, that which **burns** (the flame) is Sulfur; that which **smokes** (the volatile vapor) is Mercury; and that which remains as **ash** is Salt. This demonstration was intended to show that these three principles are present in all things, but only become visible when the body is "resolved" or broken down by fire.

### Macrocosm and Microcosm
For Paracelsus, the *tria prima* were not merely chemical ingredients but were linked to the "anatomy of nature." He believed that the Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury within the human body (the microcosm) must correspond to and be nourished by the same principles in the universe (the macrocosm) — *[Philosophy Reformed: Four Profound Tractates](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/philosophy-reformed-four-profound-tractates-paracelsus)*, [Page 156](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/philosophy-reformed-four-profound-tractates-paracelsus/page-number/156).

> "That 'like is preserved by like' should be understood in this way: namely, that the salt, sulphur, and mercury of the microcosm... is preserved by the salt, sulphur, and mercury of the macrocosm when they correspond to one another."
> — *[Philosophy Reformed: Four Profound Tractates](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/philosophy-reformed-four-profound-tractates-paracelsus)* by [Paracelsus](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/paracelsus), [Page 156](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/philosophy-reformed-four-profound-tractates-paracelsus?page=156)

q: How is the tree of the sefirot explained in the Kabbala Denudata?
label: after
final:
In Christian Knorr von Rosenroth's *Kabbala Denudata* (1677–1684), the Tree of the Sefirot is not presented as a single static diagram, but as a dynamic "Apparatus" of five universal tables (*Arbores*) that map the unfolding of the Divine from the Infinite (*Ein Sof*) into the created worlds.

### The Lurianic Framework
The explanation is rooted in the "Modern Kabbalah" of Isaac Luria. It begins with the **Or Pashut** (Simple Light) of the Infinite, followed by the **Tzimtzum** (Contraction), which creates a void for existence. From this void emerges **Adam Kadmon** (Primordial Man), the first configuration of divine light and the blueprint for the Sephirotic Tree — *[Kabbala Denudata, Tomus I](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/kabbala-denudata-tomus-i-rosenroth)* by [Christian Knorr von Rosenroth](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/christian-knorr-von-rosenroth), [Page 12](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/kabbala-denudata-tomus-i-rosenroth?page=12).

### The Five Tables (*Arbores*)
The "Explanation of the Trees" (Part IV of the *Apparatus*) details these structures as "Kabbalistic Tables" derived from sources like Naphtali Hirtz’s *Emek Ha-Melekh* (*The Valley of the King*). These tables explain:
*   **The Infinite (Ein Sof):** Described as the "simplest darkness" hidden from all eyes, which produces light through a "trace" of itself — *[Kabbala Denudata, Apparatus Pars IV](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/kabbala-denudata-seu-doctrina-hebraeorum-transcendentalis-ererah)* by [Avraham Kohen Ererah](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/avraham-kohen-ererah), [Page 252](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/kabbala-denudata-seu-doctrina-hebraeorum-transcendentalis-ererah?page=252).
*   **Anatomical Metaphors:** The Sefirot are often explained through the "parts" of the Divine Countenance (*Partzufim*), such as the **Skull** (*Karkaphta*), Ears, Nose, and Mouth, representing the different grades of light and their vessels — *[Kabbala Denudata, Tomus I](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/kabbala-denudata-tomus-i-rosenroth)* by [Christian Knorr von Rosenroth](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/christian-knorr-von-rosenroth), [Page 12](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/kabbala-denudata-tomus-i-rosenroth?page=12).

### Visual Representation
The Tree is structured into three vertical columns: **Mercy** (right), **Severity** (left), and **Harmony** (center). It maps the ten emanations—from **Kether** (Crown) at the summit to **Malkuth** (Kingdom) at the base—connected by 22 paths corresponding to the Hebrew alphabet — *[Qabbalah. The philosophical writings of Solomon Ben Yehuda Ibn…](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/qabbalah-the-philosophical-writings-of-solomon-ben-yehuda-gabirol)*, [Page 34](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/qabbalah-the-philosophical-writings-of-solomon-ben-yehuda-gabirol/page-number/34).

![Kabbala denudata sefirot](https://images.sourcelibrary.org/artwork/art-kabbala-denudata-sefirot.jpg)
*The Sephirotic Tree within nested circles of divine emanation, from the Kabbala Denudata.*

You might explore how these tables influenced the Christian Kabbalah of Henry More and Francis Mercury van Helmont, or examine the specific Zoharic "Synods" (*Idra Rabba* and *Idra Zuta*) that Rosenroth translated to explain the "Great" and "Lesser" Countenances of the Tree.

q: What do alchemical texts say about the colours of the work — black, white and red?
label: after
final:
In the alchemical tradition, the transition through the colors **black, white, and red** marks the essential progression of the Great Work (*Magnum Opus*), signifying the transformation of base matter into the Philosopher's Stone. While many intermediate colors may appear, these three are the "primary colors" that define the work's success — *[The Hermetic Museum](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/musaeum-hermeticum-1677-edition-jennis)*, [Page 450](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/musaeum-hermeticum-1677-edition-jennis/page-number/450).

### 1. Nigredo (The Blackness)
The first stage, *nigredo*, represents putrefaction, decomposition, and the "death" of the matter. It is often described as the most difficult stage to achieve, requiring a slow, steady heat to break down the substances within the sealed vessel.

*   **The Crow’s Head:** In *[The Rosary of the Philosophers](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/reg-lat-1278-anonymous)*, this stage is symbolized by the "crow's head" (*caput corvi*), signifying that the matter must rot and turn black before it can be reborn. [Page 422](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/reg-lat-1278-anonymous?page=422).
*   **Egyptian Darkness:** Eirenaeus Philalethes, in *[Ripley Reviv'd](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/ripley-reviv-d-1678-cooper)*, describes this state as "Egyptian darkness," a thick and total blackness that dominates the matter for a time. [Page 509](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/ripley-reviv-d-1678-cooper?page=509).
*   **The Black Face:** The unlettered scholar Thomas Charnock writes in the *[Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/theatrum-chemicum-britannicum-compiler)* that after a specific period of time, "Nature revealed his black face," signaling the start of the true transformation. [Page 327](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/theatrum-chemicum-britannicum-compiler?page=327).

### 2. Albedo (The Whiteness)
Once the blackness is "washed away," the matter enters the *albedo* stage. This represents purification, the "washing" of the soul, and the attainment of a silver-like clarity.

*   **The Dove:** As the matter is cleansed of its impurities, it begins to "whiten," often symbolized by a white bird or a dove. [The Rosary of the Philosophers](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/reg-lat-1278-anonymous), [Page 422](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/reg-lat-1278-anonymous?page=422).
*   **The White Face:** Charnock notes that after the blackness is overcome, the matter is made to "wash his face white and bright." [Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/theatrum-chemicum-britannicum-compiler), [Page 327](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/theatrum-chemicum-britannicum-compiler?page=327).
*   **The First Gate:** [George Ripley](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/george-ripley) explains in the *[Twelve Gates of Alchemy](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/reg-lat-1381-ripley)* that once the *nigredo* is stripped away, the body "shines" and takes on "shining white names." [Page 62](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/reg-lat-1381-ripley?page=62).

### 3. Rubedo (The Redness)
The final stage is *rubedo*, the redness that signifies perfection, the "fixed" state of the Stone, and the ultimate union of spirit and matter — *[The Hermetic Museum](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/musaeum-hermeticum-1677-edition-jennis)*, [Page 450](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/musaeum-hermeticum-1677-edition-jennis/page-number/450).

*   **The Phoenix:** The most common symbol for this stage is the phoenix, representing the final rebirth and completion of the work. [The Rosary of the Philosophers](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/reg-lat-1278-anonymous), [Page 422](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/reg-lat-1278-anonymous?page=422).
*   **Permanence:** While the black and white stages are transitory, [Eirenaeus Philalethes](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/eirenaeus-philalethes) asserts that in the *rubedo* stage, "the Stone remains in that state forever." [Ripley Reviv'd](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/ripley-reviv-d-1678-cooper), [Page 509](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/ripley-reviv-d-1678-cooper?page=509).

### Visualizing the Transformation
The *Splendor Solis* tradition, attributed to [Salomon Trismosin](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/salomon-trismosin), provides one of the most famous visual depictions of these three colors using birds within a crowned vessel.

![Three birds within a crowned glass flask, symbolizing nigredo, albedo, and rubedo.](https://images.sourcelibrary.org/archived/69593045a41e40e9146a4cc2/210.jpg)
*Emblem from [Golden Treasure Chamber](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/aureum-vellus-golden-treasure-chamber-paracelsus) by Salomon Trismosin, [Page 210](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/aureum-vellus-golden-treasure-chamber-paracelsus?page=210).*

![A white bird with three crowned heads, representing the stages of the work.](https://images.sourcelibrary.org/artwork/art-solis-splendor-solis-image-14-mars-triple-headed-bird.jpg)
*Splendor Solis. Image 14 - Mars - L'oiseau à trois têtes by Auteurs anonymes du XVIème siècle.*

### Intermediate Colors
Between these primary stages, alchemists often observed a "peacock's tail" (*cauda pavonis*) of many shifting colors. [Eirenaeus Philalethes](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/eirenaeus-philalethes) notes that two colors in particular—**green and yellow**—tend to last a long time before the white and red stages are fully realized. *[Ripley Reviv'd](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/ripley-reviv-d-1678-cooper)*, [Page 509](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/ripley-reviv-d-1678-cooper?page=509).

q: What is the green lion in alchemical texts? Show me an image of it.
label: after
final:
The **Green Lion** (*leo viridis*) is a polyvalent alchemical symbol representing the raw, "unripe" state of matter and the potent corrosive agent used to dissolve gold. In the laboratory, it is most frequently identified with **vitriol** (sulfuric acid or ferrous sulfate) or a specific "philosophical mercury" capable of breaking down the King of Metals.

### The Devouring of the Sun
The most iconic depiction of this symbol is the **Green Lion devouring the Sun**. This is an allegory for the process of *solution* or *dissolution*, where the "fixed" nature of gold (the Sun) is made "volatile" by the acidic "lion." By "eating" the sun, the lion reduces the metal to its primary, liquid essence, which is a necessary step in the creation of the Philosopher's Stone.

![The Green Lion devouring the sun](https://images.sourcelibrary.org/archived/69bd9cd86120d54bd037157c/179.jpg)
*Woodcut of the Green Lion devouring the sun from [Rosarium philosophorum](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/rosarium-philosophorum-secunda-pars-alchimiae-de-lapide-s-n-3), [Page 179](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/rosarium-philosophorum-secunda-pars-alchimiae-de-lapide-s-n-3/page-number/179).*

### Symbolic Meaning
The "greenness" of the lion has two primary interpretations in the texts:
1.  **Chemical Origin:** It refers to the green color of iron vitriol (ferrous sulfate), a key ingredient in many alchemical solvents.
2.  **Maturity:** Like green fruit, the lion represents matter that is not yet "ripe" or perfected. It is the "living" spirit of the mineral kingdom that must be tamed and matured through the alchemical fire.

As noted in a 17th-century manuscript, the image illustrates the "acid-driven dissolution of gold," where the lion's shaggy form represents the raw mineral matter containing a hidden, starry spirit.

![Green lion with stars devouring the sun](https://images.sourcelibrary.org/cropped/69b41877f1200e2ab53cf94e/69f5c4b3351d679945e1e173.jpg)
*The Green Lion grasping the sun from [Alchemical Anthology — 17th-Century German MS](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/alchemical-anthology-17th-century-german-ms-various), [Page 11](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/alchemical-anthology-17th-century-german-ms-various/page-number/11).*

### The Lion in the Great Work
In the *Rosarium philosophorum*, the lion is described as a "corrosive agent" that signifies the purification and reduction of the sun to its first matter. This process is often accompanied by the "blood" of the sun—the red liquid resulting from the gold's dissolution—which is seen as the seed of the future Tincture.

![Hand-colored Green Lion devouring the sun](https://images.sourcelibrary.org/artwork/art-lion-sun-moon.jpg)
*The Green Lion Devouring the Sun by Jaroš Griemiller (Renaissance).*

You might explore how the Green Lion transforms into the **Red Lion** in later stages of the Work, or examine the role of **vitriol** as the "secret fire" of the philosophers.

q: What did Kircher write about magnetism?
label: after
final:
Athanasius Kircher viewed magnetism as the Magical Link of the Universe, a fundamental force of attraction and sympathy that bound together all of creation, from minerals and plants to the celestial bodies and the human soul.

Athanasius Kircher (1602–1680) regarded magnetism not merely as a physical property of the lodestone, but as the fundamental "Magical Link" (*Magical Link of the Universe*) that unified all of creation. In his monumental work *[Magnes sive de Arte Magnetica](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/magnes-sive-de-arte-magnetica-kircher)* (1641), he argues that magnetism is a universal metaphor for the "hidden ties" of love and attraction that bind the cosmos together.

### The Universal Chain of Attraction
For Kircher, magnetism was the primary expression of divine providence in the material world. He described a "Magnetic Chain" (*Catena Magnetica*) that descended from God, whom he called the "Living and Eternal Magnet," down through the angels and stars to the smallest minerals. This force ensured that all things "flow together into one another with mutual charity" and naturally strive to return to their divine source — [Page 869](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/athanasii-kircheri-magnes-sive-de-arte-magnetica-opus-kircher?page=869).

### The Triple Magnet
In his later work, *[The Magnetic Kingdom of Nature](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/athanasii-kircheri-magneticum-naturae-regnum-sive-kircher)* (1667), Kircher categorized magnetism into three distinct grades:
1.  **Inanimate Magnetism:** The physical attraction found in minerals and the Earth itself — *[Magnes sive De Arte Magnetica](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/magnes-sive-de-arte-magnetica-kircher)*, [Page 759](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/magnes-sive-de-arte-magnetica-kircher/page-number/759).
2.  **Animate Magnetism:** The forces of growth and orientation in plants, such as heliotropism (the "magnetism" of the sunflower toward the sun).
3.  **Sensitive Magnetism:** The attractions, sympathies, and antipathies found in animals and humans, driven by "natural appetite" and "love" — [Page 28](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/athanasii-kircheri-magneticum-naturae-regnum-sive-kircher?page=28).

![Diagram of planetary magnetism and terrestrial apparatus](https://images.sourcelibrary.org/archived/69527376ab34727b1f04948a/691.jpg)
*This diagram from Kircher's "Magnes" illustrates 'Magnetismus Planetarum' (Planetary Magnetism) and the apparatus used to demonstrate these celestial forces on Earth — [Page 691](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/magnes-sive-de-arte-magnetica-kircher?page=691).*

### Experimental and Practical Magnetism
Kircher was a tireless experimentalist. He used a *terrella* (a spherical magnet) to model the Earth's magnetic field, demonstrating how magnetic needles change orientation based on their position relative to the poles. He also designed "magnetic wonders," including:
*   **Magnetic Clocks:** Devices that used a floating magnet or a "magnetic plant" (like a sunflower) to track the movement of the sun or moon — [Page 5](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/athanasii-kircheri-magneticum-naturae-regnum-sive-kircher?page=5).
*   **Medical Magnetism:** He believed magnets could "draw out" diseases or be used in "magnetic salves" to heal wounds through sympathy.
*   **Magnetic Geography:** Mapping the variation of the compass across the globe to assist in navigation — [Page 561](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/magnes-sive-de-arte-magnetica-kircher?page=561).

![Diagram of magnetic geography and needle orientation](https://images.sourcelibrary.org/archived/69527376ab34727b1f04948a/561.jpg)
*A diagram illustrating experiments in 'Magnetic Geography,' showing the orientation of needles relative to magnetic poles — [Page 561](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/magnes-sive-de-arte-magnetica-kircher?page=561).*

Kircher's work sought to collapse the distinction between science and magic, suggesting that what we call "magnetism" is simply the observable evidence of a universe held together by divine love.

You might follow this into Kircher's study of the "sympathetic" properties of plants in his *Mundus Subterraneus*, or explore how his magnetic theories influenced later concepts of "Animal Magnetism" in the 18th century.

q: What does Ficino say about music and the spirit?
label: after
final:
Marsilio Ficino (1433–1499), the central figure of the Florentine Academy, developed a sophisticated "musical medicine" based on the relationship between the human spirit (*spiritus*) and the vibrations of the air. For Ficino, music was not merely an aesthetic experience but a physiological and celestial tool for tuning the soul.

### The Spirit as Mediator
Ficino defines the *spiritus* as a very subtle vapor produced by the heat of the heart from the thinnest part of the blood. It acts as the essential bridge between the immaterial soul and the physical body. Because this spirit is "airy" and "mobile," it is uniquely susceptible to the "harmonically agitated air" of music — *[Phonurgia Nova](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/phonurgia-nova-kircher)*, [Page 211](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/phonurgia-nova-kircher/page-number/211). 

In his foundational work on health and astral magic, he explains that certain sounds are the primary nourishment for this spirit:

> "Indeed, the quality of this spirit is of the greatest importance to gifted individuals... Therefore, the selection of pure, luminous air, scents, and Music pertains to no one more than to them. For these three are judged to be the primary nourishments of the animal spirit."
— *[Three Books on Life](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/three-books-on-life-ficino)* by [Marsilio Ficino](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/marsilio-ficino), [Page 138](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/three-books-on-life-ficino?page=138)

### The Mechanism: Air Moving Air
Ficino’s theory of music's power rests on a "like-affects-like" principle. Since both the *spiritus* and musical sound consist of moving air, music can directly "seize" the human spirit. While the eyes perceive light (which is static), the ears perceive movement. This movement enters the body and vibrates the listener's own spirit, effectively "shaping" it to match the character of the music.

As he writes in the third book of *De vita*:

> "Remember, indeed, that song is the most powerful imitator of all things. For it imitates the intentions and affections of the soul, as well as words; it also reflects the gestures and movements of the body... It imitates and acts all these things so vehemently that it suddenly provokes both the singer and the listeners to imitate or do the same."
— *[Three Books on Life](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/three-books-on-life-1489-first-edition-ficino)* by [Marsilio Ficino](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/marsilio-ficino), [Page 159](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/three-books-on-life-1489-first-edition-ficino?page=159)

### Celestial Music and "Orphic" Singing
Ficino believed that the universe itself was a musical construct. Each planet and sphere emitted a specific tone or "Muse." By composing music that imitated the "daily positions and aspects of the stars," a practitioner could capture celestial "influxus" (influx) to heal the spirit or counteract melancholy.

*   **Solar Music:** Used to dispel the "black bile" of melancholy and bring clarity.
*   **Venusian Music:** Used to balance the spirit and inspire "honest love." — *[Declaration of Musical Instruments](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/declaracion-de-instrumentos-musicales-bermudo)*, [Page 35](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/declaracion-de-instrumentos-musicales-bermudo/page-number/35).
*   **The Muses:** Ficino mapped specific Muses to the spheres, such as Thalia to the Moon and Melpomene to the Sun, to guide the composition of these planetary hymns. — *[Le Istitutioni Harmoniche](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/le-istitutioni-harmoniche-zarlino)* by [Gioseffo Zarlino](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/gioseffo-zarlino), [Page 121](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/le-istitutioni-harmoniche-zarlino?page=121)

### Music as a Cure for Love
Later scholars like Athanasius Kircher expanded on Ficino's ideas, noting that music could even cure "love-sickness" by restoring the *temperiem* (balance) of the spirits agitated by the imagination. Ficino famously described love as a "magical" fascination occurring when two people exchange "eye-beams" and spirits, a process that could be harmonized or broken through the correct musical modes. — *[The Universal Art of Music, Volume II](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/universal-musical-work-volume-ii-musurgia-universalis-kircher)* by [Athanasius Kircher](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/athanasius-kircher), [Page 462](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/universal-musical-work-volume-ii-musurgia-universalis-kircher?page=462)

Saved to your research notebook — the *Research notebook* button under the message box on this page opens it.

You might explore how Ficino's "Orphic" singing influenced the birth of Opera in the late Renaissance, or look into his specific instructions for "drawing down" the influence of the Sun through hymns.

q: What did John Dee claim for the hieroglyphic monad in the Monas Hieroglyphica?
label: after
final:
John Dee (1527–1608/09) claimed that his Hieroglyphic Monad was a singular, universal key capable of explaining the entire cosmos through a synthesis of mathematics, magic, Kabbalah, and anagogical (mystical) interpretation. He asserted that this symbol was the "first and simplest production and representation of things," containing within its geometry the secrets of both the visible world and those things "hidden in the veils of Nature." — *[The Hieroglyphic Monad](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/the-hieroglyphic-monad-dee)*, [Page 24](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/the-hieroglyphic-monad-dee/page-number/24).

### The Construction of Unity
Dee begins his *Monas Hieroglyphica* (1564) by establishing the monad's geometric foundation. He claims that all things began from the **point** and the **monad** (unity), and that no complex form can exist without the service of this central point — *[The Hieroglyphic Monad](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/the-hieroglyphic-monad-dee)*, [Page 24](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/the-hieroglyphic-monad-dee/page-number/24).

> "By means of the straight line and the circle, the first and simplest production and representation of things was made—both of those which do not exist, and of those hidden in the veils of Nature. ... It is therefore by virtue of the point and the Monad that things first began to exist."
— *[The Hieroglyphic Monad](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/the-hieroglyphic-monad-dee)* by [John Dee](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/john-dee), [Page 24](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/the-hieroglyphic-monad-dee?page=24).

### The Components of the Monad
The symbol itself is a composite of several primary astrological and elemental signs, each of which Dee "explains" through 24 theorems:
*   **The Moon and Sun:** The top of the symbol features the crescent of the Moon joined to the circle of the Sun. Dee claims the Moon "emulates the Sun's magnitude" and "always turns its light toward the Sun," representing a master-servant relationship in the celestial hierarchy ([Page 25](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/the-hieroglyphic-monad-dee?page=25)).
*   **The Cross of the Elements:** Below the Sun sits a rectilinear cross representing the four elements (Earth, Air, Fire, Water). Dee argues that this cross can be understood as both a "Ternary" (two lines and a point) and a "Quaternary" (four lines meeting), linking the physical world to higher numerical mysteries ([Page 1031](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/theatrum-chemicum-praecipuos-selectorum-auctorum-tractatus-s-n-6?page=1031)).
*   **The Sign of Aries:** At the base of the cross are two semicircles resembling the zodiacal sign for Aries, which Dee associates with the "fire" of the alchemical process and the beginning of the Great Work — *[The Hieroglyphic Monad](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/the-hieroglyphic-monad-dee)*, [Page 2](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/the-hieroglyphic-monad-dee/page-number/2).

![The Hieroglyphic Monad symbol from the 1564 Antwerp edition.](https://images.sourcelibrary.org/archived/6952d04f77f38f6761bc4ee2/1.jpg)
*The frontispiece of [The Hieroglyphic Monad (1564 Antwerp)](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/the-hieroglyphic-monad-1564-antwerp-dee) by [Dee, John](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/john-dee), [Page 1](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/the-hieroglyphic-monad-1564-antwerp-dee?page=1).*

### Claims of Universal Power
Dee’s most ambitious claim was that the Monad was "most United" and "judged by the Magi" as the ultimate unity. He believed it was "absolutely Enriched and Endowed" with power across three distinct realms:
1.  **The Elemental World:** Governed by the cross and the four elements — *[The Hieroglyphic Monad](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/the-hieroglyphic-monad-dee)*, [Page 26](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/the-hieroglyphic-monad-dee/page-number/26).
2.  **The Celestial World:** Represented by the planetary and zodiacal components.
3.  **The Supercelestial World:** The realm of divine mysteries and "Supercelestial Revolutions" ([Page 252](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/theatrum-chemicum-praecipuos-selectorum-auctorum-tractatus-s-n-7?page=252)).

He famously claimed to have written the entire work in a twelve-day period of intense, divine inspiration while in Antwerp, viewing it as a "Divine Mystery" consigned to the "eternal monuments of letters" ([Page 56](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/the-hieroglyphic-monad-1564-antwerp-dee?page=56)).

q: What does Robert Fludd say about the macrocosm and microcosm? Show me one of his engravings.
label: after
final:
Robert Fludd (1574–1637), an Oxford-educated physician and mystical philosopher, developed a comprehensive system where the universe (the Macrocosm) and the human being (the Microcosm) are bound together by a shared divine architecture and harmonic proportions.

### The Two Worlds: Macrocosm and Microcosm
In his monumental work *[Utriusque Cosmi Historia](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/utriusque-cosmi-historia-1617-fludd)* (1617), [Robert Fludd](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/robert-fludd) defines the **Macrocosm** as the "Great World" or the entire universe, and the **Microcosm** as the "Little World" or the human being. He argues that the history of both must be understood through metaphysical, physical, and technical lenses.

Fludd asserts that the human body is a mirrored reflection of the celestial spheres. In his *[History of the Microcosm](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/tomus-secundus-de-supernaturali-naturali-praeternaturali-et-fludd-2)* (1619), he maps human faculties to cosmic hierarchies:
*   **Intellect and Reason** correspond to the supreme and middle celestial hierarchies (Angels, Archangels, and Virtues) — *[The History of the Microcosm](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/tomus-secundus-de-supernaturali-naturali-praeternaturali-et-fludd-2)*, [Page 3](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/tomus-secundus-de-supernaturali-naturali-praeternaturali-et-fludd-2/page-number/3).
*   **The Vital Light** in the heart of the Microcosm mirrors the **Sun** in the Macrocosm, which serves as the source of light and life for the universe — *[A Mytho-Hermetic Dictionary (1798)](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/a-mytho-hermetic-dictionary-1798-rainsford)* by [Charles Rainsford](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/rainsford-charles), [Page 34](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/a-mytho-hermetic-dictionary-1798-rainsford?page=34).

### The World Monochord
One of Fludd's most famous concepts is the **Monochordum Mundanum** (World Monochord). He visualizes the entire cosmos as a single-stringed musical instrument stretched from the "Earth" at the base to the highest spiritual realms at the top — *[The History of the Two Worlds](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/history-of-both-worlds-macrocosm-fludd)*, [Page 98](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/history-of-both-worlds-macrocosm-fludd/page-number/98).

> "Furthermore, here we have more precisely constructed the world monochord with its proportions, harmonies, and intervals, and we have depicted its mover as being outside the world in this manner."
> — *[Utriusque Cosmi Historia (1617)](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/utriusque-cosmi-historia-1617-fludd)* by [Robert Fludd](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/robert-fludd), [Page 99](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/utriusque-cosmi-historia-1617-fludd?page=99)

In this system, God is the "Prime Mover" who reaches out from a radiant cloud to tune the cosmic string, maintaining the "Music of the World" (*musica mundana*). The intervals of the string correspond to the elements (Earth, Water, Air, Fire) and the planetary spheres (Moon, Mercury, Venus, Sun, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn) — *[Utriusque Cosmi Historia - Tomus Primus (De Macrocosmi)](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/utriusque-cosmi-historia-tomus-primus-de-macrocosmi-fludd)* by [Robert Fludd](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/robert-fludd), [Page 92](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/utriusque-cosmi-historia-tomus-primus-de-macrocosmi-fludd?page=92).

![The World Monochord](https://images.sourcelibrary.org/archived/69904dd67d19f3f2aac1d49d/220.jpg)
*The World Monochord, depicting the human being as a 'Microcosm' perfectly mirrored within the 'Macrocosm' of the celestial spheres, from [Utriusque Cosmi Historia (1617)](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/utriusque-cosmi-historia-1617-fludd), [Page 220](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/utriusque-cosmi-historia-1617-fludd?page=220).*

### Art as the "Ape of Nature"
Fludd also introduces the concept of **Arte Naturae Simia** ("Art, the Ape of Nature"). This principle suggests that human technology and arts (such as music, geometry, and medicine) are not merely human inventions but are mimics of the creative processes found in nature. By studying these "principal daughters" of nature, man can better understand the divine mechanics of the universe — *[Utriusque Cosmi Historia (1617)](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/utriusque-cosmi-historia-1617-fludd)* by [Robert Fludd](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/robert-fludd), [Page 1](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/utriusque-cosmi-historia-1617-fludd?page=1).

You might explore Fludd's specific musical ratios in the "Symphonic Monochord," or examine his "Amphitheatre of Anatomy," where he applies these cosmic principles to the physical dissection of the human body.

### The Two Worlds: Macrocosm and Microcosm
In his monumental work *[Utriusque Cosmi Historia](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/utriusque-cosmi-historia-1617-fludd)* (1617), [Robert Fludd](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/robert-fludd) defines the **Macrocosm** as the "Great World" or the entire universe, and the **Microcosm** as the "Little World" or the human being. He argues that the history of both must be understood through metaphysical, physical, and technical lenses.

Fludd asserts that the human body is a mirrored reflection of the celestial spheres. In his *[History of the Microcosm](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/tomus-secundus-de-supernaturali-naturali-praeternaturali-et-fludd-2)* (1619), he maps human faculties to cosmic hierarchies:
*   **Intellect and Reason** correspond to the supreme and middle celestial hierarchies (Angels, Archangels, and Virtues).
*   **The Vital Light** in the heart of the Microcosm mirrors the **Sun** in the Macrocosm, which serves as the source of light and life for the universe — *[A Mytho-Hermetic Dictionary (1798)](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/a-mytho-hermetic-dictionary-1798-rainsford)* by [Charles Rainsford](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/rainsford-charles), [Page 34](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/a-mytho-hermetic-dictionary-1798-rainsford?page=34).

### The World Monochord
One of Fludd's most famous concepts is the **Monochordum Mundanum** (World Monochord). He visualizes the entire cosmos as a single-stringed musical instrument stretched from the "Earth" at the base to the highest spiritual realms at the top.

> "Furthermore, here we have more precisely constructed the world monochord with its proportions, harmonies, and intervals, and we have depicted its mover as being outside the world in this manner."
> — *[Utriusque Cosmi Historia (1617)](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/utriusque-cosmi-historia-1617-fludd)* by [Robert Fludd](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/robert-fludd), [Page 99](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/utriusque-cosmi-historia-1617-fludd?page=99)

In this system, God is the "Prime Mover" who reaches out from a radiant cloud to tune the cosmic string, maintaining the "Music of the World" (*musica mundana*). The intervals of the string correspond to the elements (Earth, Water, Air, Fire) and the planetary spheres (Moon, Mercury, Venus, Sun, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn) — *[Utriusque Cosmi Historia - Tomus Primus (De Macrocosmi)](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/utriusque-cosmi-historia-tomus-primus-de-macrocosmi-fludd)* by [Robert Fludd](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/robert-fludd), [Page 92](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/utriusque-cosmi-historia-tomus-primus-de-macrocosmi-fludd?page=92).

![The World Monochord](https://images.sourcelibrary.org/archived/69904dd67d19f3f2aac1d49d/220.jpg)
*The World Monochord, depicting the human being as a 'Microcosm' perfectly mirrored within the 'Macrocosm' of the celestial spheres, from [Utriusque Cosmi Historia (1617)](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/utriusque-cosmi-historia-1617-fludd), [Page 220](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/utriusque-cosmi-historia-1617-fludd?page=220).*

### Art as the "Ape of Nature"
Fludd also introduces the concept of **Arte Naturae Simia** ("Art, the Ape of Nature"). This principle suggests that human technology and arts (such as music, geometry, and medicine) are not merely human inventions but are mimics of the creative processes found in nature. By studying these "principal daughters" of nature, man can better understand the divine mechanics of the universe — *[Utriusque Cosmi Historia (1617)](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/utriusque-cosmi-historia-1617-fludd)* by [Robert Fludd](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/robert-fludd), [Page 1](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/utriusque-cosmi-historia-1617-fludd?page=1).

You might explore Fludd's specific musical ratios in the "Symphonic Monochord," or examine his "Amphitheatre of Anatomy," where he applies these cosmic principles to the physical dissection of the human body.

q: What does the Picatrix say about making talismans?
label: after
final:
The *Picatrix*, originally the 11th-century Arabic grimoire *Ghayat al-Hakim* ("The Goal of the Wise"), defines a talisman as a spirit within a body. It is the foundational text of "astral magic," which it describes as the science of capturing celestial power in material objects through precise timing and ritual — *[The Goal of the Wise](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/picatrix-the-goal-of-the-wise-al-majriti)*, [Page 42](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/picatrix-the-goal-of-the-wise-al-majriti/page-number/42).

### The Philosophy: A Spirit in a Body
The *Picatrix* teaches that a talisman is not merely a symbolic object but a "living body" animated by the virtues of the stars. It quotes the astronomer Thābit ibn Qurra, stating:
> "The science of images is the nobler part of astrology... those [images] which are made in due times receive the spirits and the vessels of the planets, and they become like living bodies from which wondrous effects subsequently follow."
— *[Liber Piccatriciae](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/liber-piccatriciae-picatrix-astrological-magic-al-majriti)* by [Pseudo-Maslama al-Majriti](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/maslamah-ibn-ahmad-majriti), [Page 55](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/liber-piccatriciae-picatrix-astrological-magic-al-majriti?page=55).

### The Three Requirements for Talisman-Making
To "draw down" these spirits, the practitioner must align three elements:

1.  **Astrological Timing (The Election):** The most critical factor is the "Election"—choosing the exact moment when a planet is strong. For example, a talisman for wealth requires the Moon and the Ascendant to be "fortunate" and in a harmonious aspect (trine or sextile) to the significator of the Second House (finances). — *[Picatrix (Ghāyat al-Ḥakīm)](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/picatrix-ghayat-al-hakim-attrib)*, [Page 24](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/picatrix-ghayat-al-hakim-attrib?page=24).
2.  **Material Correspondences (The Vessel):** Each planet governs specific metals and stones. Saturn rules lead and lodestone; the Sun rules gold and alumen; the Moon rules silver and crystal. The talisman must be engraved on the correct metal at the correct planetary hour. — *[The Goal of the Wise](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/picatrix-the-goal-of-the-wise-al-majriti)*, [Page 42](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/picatrix-the-goal-of-the-wise-al-majriti?page=42).
3.  **Ritual and Invocation (The Soul):** The physical object is "suffused" with power through fumigation (burning specific incenses like frankincense or sandalwood) and the recitation of planetary names or prayers to the "spiritual manifestation" of the star. — *[Picatrix (Ghāyat al-Ḥakīm)](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/picatrix-ghayat-al-hakim-attrib)*, [Page 160](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/picatrix-ghayat-al-hakim-attrib?page=160).

### Examples of Talismanic Forms
The text provides specific "images" or forms that must be engraved to achieve certain ends:
*   **For Wealth:** An image fashioned when the Tenth House and its Lord are fortunate. — [Page 24](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/picatrix-ghayat-al-hakim-attrib?page=24).
*   **For Healing:** A scorpion talisman made when the Moon enters the sign of Scorpio, used to cure stings and abdominal illnesses. — *[Three Books on Life](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/three-books-on-life-ficino-3)* by [Marsilio Ficino](https://sourcelibrary.org/author/marsilio-ficino), [Page 236](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/three-books-on-life-ficino-3?page=236).
*   **For Protection:** A figure of a turtle carved in jasper or agate and set in a lead ring to ensure the wearer is never wounded. — *[On the Magnetic Cure of Wounds](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/de-magnetica-vulnerum-curatione-goclenius)*, [Page 119](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/de-magnetica-vulnerum-curatione-goclenius?page=119).

![planetary seal](https://images.sourcelibrary.org/archived/4d4089b9-9227-4cc5-b0a2-9b06ee731061/83.jpg)
*A planetary seal for Mercury featuring an 8x8 magic square and astrological symbols, from The Egyptian Oedipus, Volume II by Athanasius Kircher, Page 83.*

![planetary personifications](https://images.sourcelibrary.org/archived/6991c5893074a1745a4119d0/91.jpg)
*The seven classical planets personified as deities, whose spirits are "drawn down" into talismans, from Sammlung Alchymistischer Schriften (German MS 3), Page 91.*

q: What do the Sanskrit texts in the collection say about purifying mercury?
label: after

In the Sanskrit alchemical tradition known as *Rasaśāstra*, mercury (*pārada* or *rasa*) is not merely a metal but the divine essence—specifically the semen—of the god Shiva.
